name: Đặng Hùng Võ
detail: Former Deputy Minister of Natural Resources and Environment; prominent advocate for real estate and second-home taxation to curb land speculation; single-asset property tax reform excluded under section 2.

name: Vũ Đình Ánh
detail: Former deputy director of Price and Market Research Institute, Ministry of Finance; advocates property taxation on real estate as a macroeconomic tool to curb speculation, but has not endorsed an annual net wealth tax.

name: Nguyễn Đức Thành
detail: Founder of VESS and former director of VEPR; led empirical evaluation of the Ministry of Finance 2018 property tax draft, warning of middle-class consumption shocks and lack of transparent asset databases; has not endorsed an annual net wealth tax.

name: Đinh Trọng Thịnh
detail: Associate Professor and senior economist at Academy of Finance; widely quoted expert on property and land tax reform to curb real estate hoarding and market distortion; single-asset property tax excluded under section 2.

name: Bộ Tài chính
detail: Authored the 2018 Draft Law on Property Tax (Dự án Luật Thuế tài sản) covering land, housing over 700m VND, cars over 1.5bn VND, aircraft, and yachts; gross physical asset and real property tax reform rather than net wealth, shelved due to public opposition.

name: Liên minh Công bằng Thuế Việt Nam
detail: Vietnam Alliance for Tax Justice (VATJ); coalition of civil society organisations and institutes advocating tax justice, corporate tax incentive reform, and transparency, but has not formally adopted an explicit wealth tax platform.

name: Phạm Minh Chính
detail: Prime Minister of Vietnam; attended 2024 G20 Summit in Rio de Janeiro and endorsed the Global Alliance Against Hunger and Poverty, but made general remarks on inclusive development and poverty reduction without an explicit wealth tax commitment.

name: Viện Nghiên cứu Kinh tế và Chính sách
detail: Vietnam Institute for Economic and Policy Research (VEPR); authored 2018 impact study evaluating draft Property Tax Law (housing over 700m VND); cautioned against regressive consumption shocks from real estate taxes, with no platform or proposal for a net wealth tax.

name: Trung tâm Thúc đẩy Giáo dục và Nâng cao Năng lực Phụ nữ
detail: Center for Education Promotion and Empowerment of Women (CEPEW); founding member of VATJ focusing on gender-responsive budgeting and corporate tax transparency; has not taken a public position on net wealth taxation.

name: Liên đoàn Thương mại và Công nghiệp Việt Nam
detail: Vietnam Chamber of Commerce and Industry (VCCI); national business federation; submitted extensive feedback on Ministry of Finance property tax proposals, advocating value-based real estate thresholds over unit counts; single-asset property tax reform excluded under section 2.

name: Hoàng Văn Cường
detail: Member of the National Assembly Committee on Finance and Budget, former Vice Rector of National Economics University (NEU); advocated property tax reform in parliamentary debates, specifically proposing second-home real estate taxes and progressive short-term transfer taxes to curb property speculation; single-asset property tax reform excluded under section 2.

name: Tổng Liên đoàn Lao động Việt Nam
detail: Vietnam General Confederation of Labour (VGCL); national trade union centre; fiscal and tax advocacy centres on raising the personal income tax family deduction threshold for workers and resisting regressive VAT increases; has not adopted a formal position calling for a statutory net wealth tax.

name: Vũ Thành Tự Anh
detail: Dean of Fulbright School of Public Policy and Management; leading public finance commentator; analyzed property taxes as an instrument for local government municipal revenues and urban land regulation, while critiquing regressive consumption taxes; has not advocated an annual net wealth tax.

name: Trung tâm Nghiên cứu Kinh tế và Chiến lược Việt Nam
detail: Vietnam Centre for Economic and Strategic Studies (VESS); economic research institute; fiscal policy studies focus on corporate income tax incentives in ASEAN and household welfare impacts of VAT, with no net wealth tax proposal.

name: Lê Quang Cường
detail: Lecturer in taxation at University of Economics Ho Chi Minh City; quoted in 2019 backing a property tax to curb real-estate speculation and expose unexplained assets; single-asset property tax, no net wealth tax.

name: Đỗ Thị Thìn
detail: Tax specialist named in a 2019 news report as agreeing with taxing the assets of the rich; report is third-person narration on a property tax, no own words or net wealth design.

name: Trương Thanh Đức
detail: Lawyer (Basico Law) at a 2018 Ministry of Finance-linked property tax workshop; proposes a progressive tax on housing and land with low thresholds; single-asset property tax.

name: Báo Đại biểu Nhân dân
detail: National Assembly daily; August 2024 article on taxing the super-rich is a Vietnamese rewrite of a Project Syndicate piece by a foreign author, not the outlet's own editorial.

name: Nguyễn Việt Cường
detail: NEU economist presenting VEPR modelling of VAT increases at a 2018 workshop; no wealth tax position. His VEPR colleague Nguyễn Đức Thành is already X0003.

name: Ban Kinh tế Trung ương
detail: Party Central Economic Commission; December 2021 forum paper by two officials suggests studying higher personal income tax on the rich to share with the poor; income tax, not a tax on wealth.
